narrative_purpose: Teaches why trees have a maximum height: with no pump, a tree pulls an unbroken thread of water up its wood; the taller it grows the more strained the column, until the topmost leaves can no longer fill and a new leaf costs more than it earns — Earth's ceiling near 122-130 m.
subject: A tall slender tree shown in clean cutaway against a dark page, with a single continuous thread of water drawn rising through the centre of its trunk from roots to crown; near the base the water thread is drawn thick, relaxed, and bright; it grows progressively thinner, more stretched, and more strained toward the top; the leaves at the very top of the tree are drawn small, dense, and shrivelled while the lower leaves are large and full; a faint dashed horizontal line crosses the upper trunk marking a ceiling the tree cannot grow past.
scene: One tall tree as a hydraulic diagram, the rising water column the clear visual subject.
camera: A flat side-on view of the whole tree, full height in frame.
light: Even diagrammatic light; the water thread glows cool and bright at the relaxed base, thinning to a tense, pale, near-breaking strand at the top; leaves brighter and fuller below, dim and shrunken above.
palette: Pandora cyan and living teal for the water thread and foliage, void-indigo trunk and background, a faint magenta tint at the strained top to read as danger.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate with strong diagrammatic clarity, hand-painted texture.
detail_level: Crisp on the rising water thread, the contrast between full lower leaves and shrivelled top leaves, and the dashed ceiling line; soft elsewhere.
composition: The tree centred, the water thread running bottom to top getting visibly thinner, the dashed ceiling near the top, open dark margins for callout labels.
consistency_notes: Earth-science figure (cohesion-tension water transport, turgor limit) in the book's cool palette; the thinning, straining water column from base to crown is the key thing that must read clearly; leave space for labels.
